messages:
jen.ciso: Heads up — new CVE I ran into during triage: CVE-2026-24876 affecting go-oauth2 (token refresh) and changes in net/http connection reuse. looks like it could leak tokens under certain idle/keepalive patterns. tagging eng and platform.

matt-eng: ugh. where did this come from? any public exploit PoC yet?

jen.ciso: No public PoC. NVD entry + upstream advisory. severity: High by impact, but exploit complexity medium. it interacts badly with grpc proxying in a few service patterns we use.

ravi-sre: @jen.ciso can you paste the advisory? i'll run quick binary search across services and list repos with vulnerable go.mod references.

jen.ciso: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xxxx-yyyy

jen.ciso: quick snippet of vulnerable lines we saw in internal logs:```\nmodule github.com/redwood/inference\n\nrequire (\n    github.com/coreos/go-oidc v0.8.0 // vulnerable\n    google.golang.org/grpc v1.54.0\n)\n```\n
sara-platform: I saw a few services pinned to go-oidc v0.8 in staging and prod feature branches. these are the ones behind token refresh endpoints: auth-service, orchestrator, streaming-proxy.

matt-eng: recommend triage score matrix: impact to tokens (3), exploitability (2), reach (2) => priority = 7/9 => treat as P0 for auth-service, P1 for others. propose hotpatch to auth-service today.

kevin-rls: agree. i'd add we should pin and backport for our maintained branches (v1.6.x, v1.7.x). we should also enable an automated go mod tidy + replace in the PR to force the safer version.

ravi-sre: operational asks: can we canary the fix behind a feature flag and enable audit logging for token refresh paths so we can detect regressions? also rotate KMS keys for short window if we suspect token leakage.

jen.ciso: KMS rotation might be overkill immediately. let's rotate if we see anomalous audit logs. but yes, add detailed audit logs for refresh endpoints and run canary.

matt-eng: patch plan I propose:
1) create branch hotfix/oauth-cve-2149999999 in auth-service
2) bump go-oidc to v0.9.2 (upstream fixed) in go.mod + run `go mod tidy`
3) add unit test that simulates conn reuse shuffle (see repro harness)
4) backport to v1.7.x and v1.6.x with cherry-picks
5) deploy canary to 1% prod, monitor audit logs and error budget for 30 minutes, then 25% and 100%

matt-eng: example go.mod diff to include in PR description:
```diff
-require github.com/coreos/go-oidc v0.8.0
+require github.com/coreos/go-oidc v0.9.2
```

kevin-rls: i'll open the backport PRs after auth-service PR merges. also suggest we add a module-override in our internal monorepo CI for the duration so other services get the fixed module in CI runs: `replace github.com/coreos/go-oidc => github.com/coreos/go-oidc v0.9.2`

ravi-sre: for grpc interaction: some proxies use google.golang.org/grpc interceptors that touch context tokens. we should scan for usages of `context.Value("token")` patterns and add quick runtime checks in the canary to ensure no token propagation anomalies.

jen.ciso: Good. also update the security tracker: add CVE ID, affected services list, mitigation steps, PR links, responsible owners, and timeline. I'll coordinate customer-facing comms if needed.

patchbot: Deploy job queued: auth-service/hotfix/oauth-cve-2149999999 -> staging.

matt-eng: i'll start the PR now and tag reviewers: @sara-platform for canary config, @ravi-sre for monitoring, @kevin-rls for backports. target short SLA: PR by EOD, canary by tomorrow morning.

sara-platform: FYI we need to run compatibility tests for net/http keepalive semantics with the updated version — i'll allocate a couple of hours on the infra CI matrix.

jen.ciso: thanks team. keep updates here. if we detect anything odd in audit logs after canary, we rotate keys. :thumbsup:

matt-eng: PR opened: https://git.redwood.dev/auth-service/pulls/392 (WIP)

ravi-sre: scan results: found 8 repos referencing old module directly. i'll paste list to the tracker.

kevin-rls: note for release notes: mark as security hotfix, CVE-2026-24876, mention recommended client upgrades for customers on self-hosted bundles.

jen.ciso: Good. closing loop: after 24h of stable canary, we do mass rollout and close the ticket.

matt-eng: noted.
